summary: A summary of replies to the query in RFC 473 about MIX and MIXAL tools on the ARPANET. It lists rumored interpreters at Utah and Stanford, a MIXAL assembler and partly debugged interpreter at UCSB, and MIX and MIXAL on the UCSD B6700.

plainLanguage.summary: A list of which network computers could run the pretend computer from a famous book, split into rumors and facts.

questions: where could mix run on the arpanet
subtitle: A summary of replies on where Knuth's MIX computer and its MIXAL assembler could be used on the ARPANET.

tldr.problem: David Walden had asked in RFC 473 whether assemblers and interpreters existed for Knuth's hypothetical MIX computer.
tldr.mechanism: He summarizes the responses, separating rumors from facts and naming the sites and contacts.
tldr.outcome: MIX and MIXAL were reported available at UCSB, UCSD and UCLA, with rumors for Utah and SU-AI.

today: The status in the unit data is Unknown. It is a snapshot of April 1973 availability and not a standard.

sections.title: Rumors
sections.content: This RFC summarizes responses to the request in RFC 473 for information on assemblers and interpreters for Knuth's hypothetical MIX computer. There are two rumors: a MIX interpreter, but no assembler, on the University of Utah PDP-10, and a MIX interpreter on the SU-AI PDP-10.
sections.plainLanguage: Some people only heard that a computer might have the program, so the author labels those as rumors.

sections.title: Confirmed Availability
sections.content:
A fairly well debugged and documented MIXAL assembler exists for the UCSB 360/75, with a partially debugged MIX interpreter; RFC 485 has details.

MIX and MIXAL are available on the UCSD B6700, though not handled as fully supported products and possibly with remaining bugs. Contact Ken Bowles at UCSD. MIX and an assembler are available on the UCLA 360/91, documented and with considerable use. Contact Bob Braden at CCN.
sections.plainLanguage: Three places said for sure they had it, and each has a person to ask.

sections.title: Stanford Package
sections.content: Finally, the Computer Science Center at Stanford University apparently has a standard package for exporting the MIX systems to 360s and 370s.
sections.plainLanguage: One more place may have a kit for copying it onto other computers.

references.text: Walden, D., NWG/RFC 473, the MIX query.
Pickens, J., "MIX and MIXAL at UCSB", RFC 485, March 1973.
